parts.txt: Commonly known as RPE, the Rate of Perceived Exertion is a simple yet powerful tool for measuring one's physical exertion during an exercise session. Unlike other metrics, RPE is subjective and based on how you feel, both physically and mentally, making it unique to each individual.
This subjective approach makes RPE a valuable metric for those looking to self-regulate their training and use their instincts, rather than relying on data measurements.
More on Training to Heart Rate
The Modified Borg Scale
The modified Borg scale is the most commonly used scale for measuring RPE. This ranges from 0 to 10, with '0' representing no exertion and '10' representing maximum effort.
10 / Max Effort
Feels almost impossible to continue. Completely out of breath and unable to talk. Only sustainable for a very short time.
9 / Very Hard
Extremely difficult to maintain. Breathing is very heavy and you can only speak a few words.
7–8 / Vigorous
Uncomfortable effort. Short of breath, but you can still speak in short sentences.
4–6 / Moderate
Breathing more heavily. You can hold a short conversation, but the effort is becoming noticeably challenging.
2–3 / Light
Comfortable and easy. You could maintain this pace for hours while breathing normally and chatting.
1 / Very Light
Minimal exertion — more than resting, but still extremely easy.
When to Use RPE
At Runna, we generally recommend following your pace targets as these are the clearest way to track your progress and practise your pacing ahead of race day.
However, we encourage you to use RPE in the following circumstances:
When you’re feeling more fatigued than usual
In difficult weather conditions (heat, wind, high humidity)
On hilly routes
On trails or technical terrain
At altitude
After illness, or when returning from injury

With all of these factors, your body will have to work much harder to hit your pace targets and this will require more effort. Using RPE in these situations allows you to focus on getting the session done at the right intensity, ensuring your training remains enjoyable, effective and sustainable.

Please note that Pace Analysis won’t be available for workouts completed using RPE. Since RPE is a subjective measure of effort, it doesn’t provide a comparable performance metric in the same way pace does.
How to Use RPE in Your Runna Workout
Head to your Profile in the Runna app (top left-hand corner)
Select Units of Measure
Select RPE
Re-sync your watch connection to pull through your changes!
Top Tips for Using RPE

Gauging your RPE can feel tricky at first, but with practice it becomes much easier to match how you feel to a number on the scale. This can be especially helpful on race day - if GPS is weak and audio cues are inaccurate, knowing what your race effort feels like can help you stay consistent and avoid starting too hard.

A handy way to gauge your RPE while running is the talk test. At a very light effort, you should be able to comfortably hold a conversation. As the intensity increases, talking becomes harder and you’ll only be able to speak in shorter phrases.
As your fitness and strength builds, paces that felt hard at the start of a training block will begin to feel easier - giving you a lower RPE for the same pace!
FAQs
I've selected RPE in the Runna app, so why I am still seeing pace target screens on my compatible smartwatch?
Unfortunately, most smartwatches don’t currently support displaying RPE-based workouts. In these cases, your watch will still show Runna’s default workout screen, which includes pace targets.
If you’d prefer not to see pace targets, you can disable pace or audio cues in your watch’s native settings.
Will I receive Pace Insight Recommendations if I complete my workouts using RPE?

Pace Analysis won’t be available for workouts completed using RPE. Since RPE is a subjective measure of effort, it doesn’t provide a comparable performance metric in the same way pace does. However, you're more than welcome to switch to and from RPE and pace targets depending on your workout!

title: What Are Pace Insight Recommendations and How Do They Work?

parts.txt: What Are Pace Insights?

Pace Insights are a feature that help us assess your current performance and tailor your training plan to your ability. This personalisation helps to ensure that your training remains effective, sustainable and enjoyable!
How Do Pace Insights Work?

We compare how you’re performing in your speed sessions (Intervals, tempo runs and time trials). We'll compare the paces you achieve with the paces set in your plan, and we monitor how consistent you are within and between workouts. If we detect a clear trend, we’ll suggest a recommendation to bring your training paces in line with your current performance.
You should receive a Pace Status update after any speed session. If you can’t see this, please check the FAQs below for support.
How Do I Access Pace Insights?
You’ll find Pace Insights in the Plan tab of your Runna app. There, you’ll see a status card based on how your recent speed sessions are going:
Pace on Point: You’re perfectly on track with your plan.
Ahead of the Pack: You’re ahead of your plan. Tap 'View update' to see your recommended pace change.
Let’s Review Your Pace: A pace decrease may make training more effective and enjoyable. Tap 'View update' to see your recommended pace change.
Variable Pace Detected: We can’t make a recommendation just yet as your results have been mixed. Focus on hitting your pace targets and staying consistent!

Monitoring Your Pace Data: We don’t have enough data yet, so you'll receive this when you're new to a plan or you've recently updated your paces. Complete your next interval, tempo or time trial session to generate more data!
FAQs
Do I have to accept my pace target recommendation?

If you do receive a pace change recommendation, you don’t have to accept it. While it’s based on your recent performance, we can’t account for factors like weather, undulating terrain, poor sleep, or inadequate fuelling just yet. You're in control, so take a look at our Pace Insights chart and interpret the recommendations as you see fit!
Will my plan change if I accept a pace recommendation shift?

Yes, but the only thing that will change is your pace targets! Your plan will remain exactly the same, and Runna will update the pace targets throughout your plan to better align with your current ability.
Remember that easy runs should always feel comfortable and conversational, regardless of any pace changes!
I didn't accept my pace recommendation shift - how can I change my pace targets?
No worries! You can either continue with your plan and wait for another pace recommendation after your next speed workout, or adjust your pace targets manually.
To update your paces manually in the Runna app:
Go to the Plan tab
Tap Manage Plan
Scroll down to Estimated Race Time
We recommend adjusting your estimated race time by 20–30 seconds at a time to avoid making large changes to your target paces too quickly.
Why are my pace recommendations inconsistent?

If you think you’re hitting your target paces during your speed workouts, inconsistent recommendations could be due to an unstable GPS signal. Pace Insights rely on your device’s GPS, so poor signal can sometimes lead to conflicting pace recommendations.
To help improve accuracy, please check the following:
Make sure Low Power Mode isn’t enabled on your phone or watch.
Try to avoid running in areas with large buildings or poor signal coverage that could interfere with GPS.
Ensure Runna has all the required location and background permissions:On iOS: Settings → General → Background App RefreshOn Android: turn off any battery optimisation settings for the Runna app.
On iOS: Settings → General → Background App Refresh
On Android: turn off any battery optimisation settings for the Runna app.
Check that you’re not using another GPS-based app at the same time (such as Strava or other fitness tracking apps).
Why has my card been saying 'Monitoring Your Pace Data' for multiple weeks?
There are a few possible reasons for why you may not have received a Pace Insight:

Workouts have been recorded manually:Make sure you’re recording your workouts directly through the Runna app on your phone, or with the Runna workout on your smartwatch. Unfortunately, 'free runs' and manual uploads cannot be used for pace analysis.
Pace targets are turned off:Go to Profile (top left) → Workout Settings and check that Pace Targets are switched on.
You recently updated your estimated race time:Updating your estimated race time will reset your Pace Status, so you’ll need to complete more speed sessions before receiving an update.

Inconsistent or in-complete workout data:Pace Insights rely on consistent data to provide a true recommendation, so aim to complete your workouts as planned, including the warm-up, cool down and any planned reps. If your warm-up is going to differ from the planned distance, head to your Profile → Workouts and tick Open Warm-Up.
After making any changes to your Runna settings, you'll need to refresh any third-party app and watch connections (e.g Garmin or COROS) via Bluetooth.

title: The Importance of a Deload Week

parts.txt: Training hard all of the time is not only unachievable, but also taxing on the body. Running at a high intensity every session can build cumulative fatigue within the body and lead to increased risk of injury, as well as being mentally fatiguing.​Introducing: the deload week. The quiet and supportive training partner all athletes need.
What is a deload week?
A deload week is a period of time strategically designed to reduce the volume or intensity of training to allow the body to recover – and come back to training even stronger.

The concept can intimidate some runners as they may worry they'll lose their fitness, but in reality it actually does the complete opposite. You may hear of some runners dreading the taper for similar reasons – but these periods are just as essential to an optimal training plan as any hard session! Relax – You’re not going backwards. Trust the process.
Why include a deload week?
It allows your body to make physiological adaptations from your recent training sessions
It provides you with a mental refresh, so you can look forward to getting back into your next block of training
It will allow you to truly overcome underlying fatigue in the body, reducing injury risk
If you complete deload weeks correctly and ensure that you listen to your body, you will feel more energised, in turn finding yourself improving quicker.
Recovery

Take the extra time that you gain in a deload week to focus on your body's recovery. Read our below article where we've covered our top-tips to recover from your tougher sessions as quickly as possible and keep those injuries at bay.

title: Use Not Feeling 100% to Adjust Your New to Running, Return to Running, and Path to parkrun Plan

parts.txt: Feeling under the weather, dealing with an ache, or just hit a really busy week?
This is exactly when adjusting your training can help you stay consistent long term. A short step back now often means a stronger, more confident return later.
This guide is specific to New to Running, Return to Running, and Path to parkrun plans, where progression is gradual and consistency matters more than pushing through.
Why Adjusting Your Training Matters
When life gets busy or your body’s not feeling quite right, your ability to recover takes a hit.
That might look like:
Poor sleep
Higher stress levels
Less time to properly fuel or rest
Lingering fatigue or small aches
Trying to train as normal during these periods can make everything feel harder than it should, and in some cases, lead to burnout or injury which we want to avoid.
This is when it’s key to pick up on those signals and change your training accordingly. Adjusting your plan is protecting the progress you’ve made so far, not losing progress.
When Should You Adjust?
You don’t need to wait until things feel really bad.
Consider using Not Feeling 100% to adjust your training if:
You can see a particularly busy or stressful week ahead
Your sleep has frequently dropped below your normal baseline
You’re feeling unusually fatigued or unmotivated
You’ve picked up a minor ache or illness
Running feels harder than it normally does at the same effort
Choosing the Right Adjustment
For New to Running, Return to Running, and Path to parkrun plans, your plan adjustment comes down to one simple question:
Do you need a full break, or just a lighter week?
Option 1: Reduced Running
Best for:
Busy weeks where you still have some time to run
Mild fatigue or low energy
Slight dips in sleep or increased stress
Wanting to maintain routine without overdoing it
This option keeps you moving, but lowers the overall load so your body can keep up.
The options you’ll see depend on how many runs you currently have in your plan:

rows: Runs per week in your plan

parts.txt: Option 2: No Running
Best for:
Minor illness or feeling run down
Persistent aches or pains
Very low energy or poor sleep over several days
Taking a short break can help your body properly recover, rather than dragging fatigue forward.
When you’re off for a longer period of time, you’ll ease in gradually with a short return phase to help you rebuild safely.
How Quickly Should You Come Back?
If you take time off, you’ll choose how gently to return:
Balanced: A steady return if you’re feeling mostly back to normal
Slow: A more gradual rebuild if you want to be extra cautious or you’re not 100% yet
There’s no “right” answer here, it just depends on how you’re feeling.
A Few Things to Keep in Mind
Not Feeling 100% adjustments are designed for short-term changes (up to 14 days)
If you need longer, it’s better to restart with a fresh plan when you’re ready
Always listen to your body, it’s your best guide
This guidance is based on coaching best practices and isn’t a substitute for medical advice. If something doesn’t feel right, it’s always worth speaking to a professional.
Scaling Back Doesn’t Mean You’re Losing Progress
Listening to your body is the right move, and you shouldn’t feel like doing so compromises any of your hard work! A few missed or reduced runs won’t undo your progress.

In fact, adjusting at the right time is often what keeps runners consistent over weeks and months. Pushing through when your body (or life) isn’t ready is far more likely to set you back in the long run.]
Training isn’t about being perfect every week, it’s about showing up consistently over time. Adjust when you need to, and trust that you’ll come back stronger.

title: How Is My Target Race Time Predicted?

parts.txt: Note: some runners may not see an estimated race time in-app for plans that have unpredictable variables in your chosen race (e.g., terrain, hills).
Your race time prediction is based on the metrics that you've told us, such as your running ability and training schedule as well as all of the data that we've seen from runners just like you.

Please note that this is an estimation and on your race day, you may be faster or slower than we predict. The best thing that you can do is to follow all of the sessions in your plan and assuming that you avoid injury, we'd expect you to finish somewhere in this range.
Lots of Runnas also exceed the range that we predict, so don't feel limited by the race time predictions either.
Adjusting Your Plan for a Specific Goal Race Time

If you're training for a new goal, such as a Half-Marathon or Marathon and have a target goal in mind, we want to help you get there! You can view your estimated target time in your 'Plan Introduction' and when clicking on the Race workout from within your Runna plan. Three things to consider:
It's important to note that this is an estimated time and you could run faster or slower than we predict.
Our prediction is assuming good running conditions and a relatively flat road course.
We've tried to be conservative where possible to give you the best chance of achieving the fastest time that we estimate for you.
What if You Want a Faster Predicted Race Time?

If you're wanting to train for a race time that is faster than what we've estimated for you, you'll need to increase your estimated race time at the current week of your plan. You can either do this when starting your plan (which will make your initial pace targets harder) or during your plan.
You can also achieve this by regularly running faster than your suggested paces during the speed sessions in your plan.

Our Pace Insights will notify you that you're "Ahead of the Pack" and provide you with an adjusted pace recommendation which you can choose to accept, making the rest of your plan incrementally faster, or continue with your original pace recommendations.
Good luck in your race!
If you'd like more information on adjusting your paces including your target race time, please read our support article on how to adjust your estimated current race time.

title: How to Use and Manage Your Target Mileage Settings on Run Further and Train Your Way Plans

parts.txt: Why Target Mileage Matters

Your target mileage defines the goals you’ll work toward throughout your training plan. By specifying the weekly and long-run distances you’d like to reach, you give Runna a clear finishing line, so we can build a plan that takes you from today’s baseline to your desired level.
How Target Mileage Affects Your Plan

When you enter your target mileage, we treat those numbers as the distances you aim to complete by the final week of your plan. While we can’t promise to hit those exact figures—since factors like your ability level, preferred run days, and plan length also influence progression—your targets set the tone for each phase of the plan. We structure your plan into three-week progression blocks, each followed by a lighter “deload” week to help your body recover and adapt, keeping you strong and injury-free.
Weekly Mileage vs. Long-Run Target
Weekly mileage represents the total distance you hope to accumulate over seven days (Monday–Sunday). Longest run target is the single-run distance you’re working toward in those same seven days.
Determining Your Target Mileage

Runna offers smart default targets based on your current mileage, ability level, and plan length. If you’re unsure what to set, feel free to leave these defaults as-is—our plan will guide your progression safely. Your plan will also adapt automatically for holidays, travel, or busy weeks, ensuring you stay on track even when life gets hectic.

If you’d rather choose your own targets, use a gradual build-up: increase your weekly mileage by no more than 10%–15% above your current average, and pick a long-run distance that feels challenging but achievable. Think about any future running goals—what peak distance will you need down the road?—and set your longest run accordingly. Factor in your schedule (vacations, busy weeks) and round to the nearest mile for simplicity.
How to Adjust Mileage Bounds
Go to Plan
Tap Manage Plan
Under Target, select either Weekly Mileage to change Target Weekly Mileage or Longest Run to change your Target Longest Run.
Tap Update

If your chosen targets fall outside the allowable range, you may need to update your ability level or the number of days you plan to run each week. Runna uses those parameters to cap safe progression rates: raising your run-day count or ability unlocks higher targets, while reducing them lowers the ceiling.

By carefully selecting and reviewing your target mileage, you’ll empower Runna to craft a personalized training progression that bridges today’s fitness to tomorrow’s achievements. Lace up and let’s go!

title: How to Use and Manage Your Target Mileage Settings on a Run to Maintain Plan

parts.txt: Why Target Mileage Matters

The target mileage on a Run to Maintain is your steady-state weekly volume—the distance you want to sustain throughout your plan. By entering one consistent mileage figure, you help Runna keep you fit and strong between training blocks, avoiding spikes or drops that can lead to fatigue or injury.
How Target Mileage Affects Your Plan

Runna uses your target mileage as the core volume each week, allowing workouts to fluctuate by a small percentage (up or down) to introduce variety while holding you near your chosen level. Rather than building toward a new peak, your plan focuses on maintaining fitness, reinforcing your aerobic base, and sharpening speed or endurance at your current capability.
Weekly Mileage vs. Longest Run

Weekly mileage is the total distance you cover in seven days (usually Monday–Sunday). Your longest run is the single most extended session within that same period and contributes directly to your weekly total. In a Run to Maintain Plan, Runna uses both of these inputs to design each week’s volume and the length of your long run.
Determining Your Target Mileage

If you’re unsure what to put as your target mileage you can use the default options that Runna recommends or use your average from the last four weeks for both weekly mileage and longest run. Being honest ensures your plan challenges you without overreaching.
How to Adjust Your Target Mileage
If you need to tweak your target mileage — because your schedule changes, you’re feeling stronger, or you simply want to maintain a different volume — you can update this with the following steps:
Go to Plan
Tap Manage Plan
Under Target, select either Weekly Mileage to change Target Weekly Mileage or Longest Run to change your Target Longest Run.
Tap Update
Once updated, Runna will adjust your weekly targets while preserving the same deload structure.

If you see an error message indicating that your target mileage is above or below the allowable range, you’ll need to update your Running Ability level or the number of Runs Per Week. Runna uses those settings to cap safe progression and ensure your plan remains sustainable and injury-free.
How to Change Target Mileage Back: Go to Plan → tap Manage Plan → under Target, select Weekly Mileage or Longest Run → enter your original values → tap Update.

title: What are Pace Insights and How do They Work?

parts.txt: What Are Pace Insights?

Pace Insights are a feature that help us assess your current performance and tailor your training plan to your ability. This personalisation helps to ensure that your training remains effective, sustainable and enjoyable!
How Do Pace Insights Work?

We compare how you’re performing in your sessions with pace targets (Intervals, tempo runs, time trials and some long runs). We'll compare the paces you achieve with the paces set in your plan, and we monitor how consistent you are hitting those targets. ​
If we detect a clear trend, we’ll suggest a recommendation to bring your training paces in line with your current performance.
You should receive a Pace Status update after any session with pace targets. If you can’t see this, please check the FAQs below for support.
How Do I Access Pace Insights?
You’ll find Pace Insights in the Plan tab of your Runna app. There, you’ll see a status card based on how your recent speed sessions are going:
Pace on Point: You’re perfectly on track with your plan.
Ahead of the Pack: You’re ahead of your plan. Tap 'View update' to see your recommended pace change.

Variable Pace Detected: We can’t make a recommendation just yet as your results have been mixed. Focus on hitting your pace targets and staying consistent!

Monitoring Your Pace Data: We don’t have enough data yet, so you'll receive this when you're new to a plan or you've recently updated your paces. Complete your next interval, tempo or time trial session to generate more data!
⚠️ Pace Insights are not available on New to Running, Return to Running, or Path to parkrun plans.
FAQs
Do I have to accept my pace target recommendation?
No, you're always in control. Pace Insights never automatically change your training paces without your input. If you receive a recommendation:
You can choose to apply the change
If you don't accept it, nothing changes — your plan stays exactly the same
You can revert changes later if you change your mind

While recommendations are based on your recent performance, we can't yet account for factors like weather, terrain, poor sleep, or fuelling. Take a look at your Pace Insights chart and interpret them as you see fit!
Will my plan change if I accept a pace recommendation shift?

Yes, but the only thing that will change is your pace targets! Your plan will remain exactly the same, and Runna will update the pace targets throughout your plan to better align with your current ability.
Remember that easy runs should always feel comfortable and conversational, regardless of any pace changes!
Can I undo or revert a pace insight change I accepted?
Yes, you can revert an accepted pace insight manually by going to Plan → Manage Plan → Current Race Times (adjust in 15–30 sec increments).
Does my plan adapt automatically?

The only way your plan adapts is via Pace Insights, which monitors your speed sessions and guides pace adjustments. After each workout that has pace targets (Intervals, tempo runs, time trials and some long runs), you'll receive a Pace Status. If Pace Insights spots a consistent pattern between eligible sessions, it may suggest you speed up or slow down. Accepting a recommendation is what actually updates your plan, nothing changes without your input.
Inside the Plan tab, you’ll find the pace insights area that breaks everything down:
Why you received your latest status
Which workouts contributed to it
Whether you want to accept or reject any recommendations

You’ll also see a chart showing your five most recent speed workouts, with all reps standardised so you can compare different distances. It highlights how steady you’ve been and where you’ve gone above or below your target paces.
If a run isn’t eligible, the app will explain why and tell you what to do next so more of your future sessions count.
I didn't accept my pace recommendation shift - how can I change my pace targets?
No worries! You can either continue with your plan and wait for another pace recommendation after your next speed workout, or adjust your pace targets manually.
To update your paces manually in the Runna app:
Go to the Plan tab
Tap Manage Plan
Scroll down to Estimated Race Time
We recommend adjusting your estimated race time by 20–30 seconds at a time to avoid making large changes to your target paces too quickly.
Why are my pace recommendations inconsistent?

If you think you’re hitting your target paces during your speed workouts, inconsistent recommendations could be due to an unstable GPS signal. Pace Insights rely on your device’s GPS, so poor signal can sometimes lead to conflicting pace recommendations.
To help improve accuracy, please check the following:
Make sure Low Power Mode isn’t enabled on your phone or watch.
Try to avoid running in areas with large buildings or poor signal coverage that could interfere with GPS.
Ensure Runna has all the required location and background permissions:On iOS: Settings → General → Background App RefreshOn Android: turn off any battery optimisation settings for the Runna app.
On iOS: Settings → General → Background App Refresh
On Android: turn off any battery optimisation settings for the Runna app.
Check that you’re not using another GPS-based app at the same time (such as Strava or other fitness tracking apps).
Why has my card been saying 'Monitoring Your Pace Data' for multiple weeks?
There are a few possible reasons for why you may not have received a Pace Insight:

Workouts have been recorded manually:Make sure you’re recording your workouts directly through the Runna app on your phone, or with the Runna workout on your smartwatch. Unfortunately, 'free runs' and manual uploads cannot be used for pace analysis.
Pace targets are turned off:Go to Profile (top left) → Workout Settings and check that Pace Targets are switched on.
You recently updated your estimated race time:Updating your estimated race time will reset your Pace Status, so you’ll need to complete more speed sessions before receiving an update.

Inconsistent or in-complete workout data:Pace Insights rely on consistent data to provide a true recommendation, so aim to complete your workouts as planned, including the warm-up, cool down and any planned reps. If your warm-up is going to differ from the planned distance, head to your Profile → Workouts and tick Open Warm-Up.
After making any changes to your Runna settings, you'll need to refresh any third-party app and watch connections (e.g Garmin or COROS) via Bluetooth.
Are walk/runs eligible for pace insights?
No walk runs are not eligible for pace insights. Sessions that can have pace insights include intervals, tempo runs, time trials, and some long runs.
Need more help?
If you have more questions about pace insights, reach out via the in-app support tab and our team will be happy to help!

We know that training doesn’t always fit neatly into a structured plan. Maybe you’ve signed up for a last-minute race, or you’re in between training blocks and just feel like pushing yourself with a sharp interval session.

That’s exactly why we created Instant Workouts. They’re designed to give you the freedom to train whenever and however you want, without being tied to a full plan. Whether you’re looking for a quick fitness boost, a specific session to match your mood, or a workout that fits around your day, Instant Workouts put you in complete control.

With the flexibility to choose what you need, when you need it, you can run entirely on your own terms - while still getting the structure and quality of a purposeful session. Ultimate control, total freedom and training that works around you!
What Can You Do with Instant Workouts?
With Instant Workouts, you can:
Choose any workout, any time: Pick from the full Runna workout library - from intervals to tempo runs to easy efforts and add extra sessions on top of your plan
Set your own goals: Train your way by targeting time, distance, or pace
Seamlessly track your progress: Every workout is logged in your Training Calendar automatically, so you can see your consistency build over time and track what you’ve done at a glance.
How Do I Use Instant Workouts?
Getting set up is quick and simple:
Open the Runna app and scroll to the bottom of your Today Tab, or tap into your Calendar tab
Select “Add Run.”
Choose the workout type that fits your needs: easy run, long run, intervals, tempo, race or parkrun workout.
Set your preferences: time, distance, or pace targets.
Hit Start, make sure your audio cues are enabled and follow your personalised guidance!
When Should I Use Instant Workouts?
Instant Workouts are ideal when you want a little extra flexibility, for example:
Fitting in extra training around a busy schedule
Trying something new outside of your regular plan
Adding variety to your weekly routine
Think of Instant Workouts as your on-demand training companion - ready whenever you are!
Do I Need Instant Workouts?
You definitely don't need to add Instant Workouts, but they let you complement your plan with spontaneous sessions tailored to your goals. They’re perfect for:
Spontaneous race workouts
Social runs with friends
Parkrun
Fitting in a shorter session over your lunch break or whilst you're on holiday!
It’s flexibility, without losing the quality of a purposeful workout.
FAQs
Can I record a parkrun with Instant Workouts?

Yes! parkrun is a great way to get your weekly 5K in - whether you’re chasing a PB or keeping it social. With Instant Workouts, you can record your parkrun and have it automatically logged alongside your training.
To log your parkrun:
Go to Instant Workouts at the bottom of the Today Tab in the Runna app.
Select parkrun from the list.
Hit Start and get running.
Your parkrun will automatically sync to your Training Calendar in Calendar tab, contributing to your weekly mileage and helping you track your progress over time.
Is Instant Workouts available to all users?
Instant Workouts is a Premium feature. Upgrade to access this and more. If you’re not a Premium subscriber, you’ll still get one complimentary workout to try it out.
Can I use Instant Workouts for non-running activities?
Not right now - Instant Workouts are currently available for runs only. We’re working on expanding this to other activities, so stay tuned!
Will Instant Workouts affect my main training plan?

No - Instant Workouts are designed to complement your plan, not replace it. Any workouts you complete will still be logged in your Training Calendar in the Calendar tab, so you get a complete view of your training and progress.
Can I do my own custom running sessions or interval workouts?

No, you can't fully design your own custom workouts. Instant Workouts let you add extra sessions to your plan at any time (Easy Runs, Intervals, Tempo runs and more). You can choose your preferred distance or duration and pick from the full Runna workout library. You can access Instant Workouts via the Today tab (scroll to the bottom) or through the Calendar tab.
Need further support?
If you have any questions or need more support, please reach out via the in-app support channel and we'll do our best to help!

title: Your Quick Guide to Navigating the Runna App

parts.txt: Runna is designed to help you reach your training goals with a fully customizable, easy-to-navigate app. But for those who want to dive deeper into Runna’s coolest features, this guide will walk you through the tools you can use to tailor your plan to fit your needs and stay on track.
Your Profile
Your hub for shoes, subscriptions, preferences, and settings.
View your Runna Level: Scroll down to see your exclusive offers.
Add your shoes: Track your mileage so you know when it’s time to replace them.
Add your parkrun barcode: Race, easy run, or tempo effort - everything you need to track your parkrun efforts!
Subscription details: View your Runna Premium subscription details
Workout & Phone Recording Settings: Running on the track? Enable Open Warm-Up and Intervals/Tempo on Track, choose your pace target preferences, and customise your audio cues.
Heart Rate Zones: View and adjust your heart rate zones to better understand your training.
Runna Labs: Get early access to new features and share your feedback!
Language & Notification Preferences: Set your language and manage notifications.
Find a Race: Discover upcoming races with Race Discovery.
Listen to the Runna Podcast: Available on multiple listening platforms - we’ve got you covered!
Get featured on our socials: Completed your first long run with friends or smashed a PB? Tell us about it for a chance to be featured on our socials!
The Today Tab
The Today tab is your one-stop shop for everything you need to stay on track with your training each day:
Workout details: See exactly what’s planned for the day - whether it’s a run, strength session, or rest day.
Expert tips: Get helpful insights to make the most of your workout.
Weekly mileage: View your total mileage for the week at a glance.
Add an Instant Workout: choose tailored sessions to fit your immediate needs.
View the Plan Adjustment Tray: had a busy few weeks and missed some workouts? Align your training to to get you back on track.
With everything in one place, the Today tab keeps you prepared, focused, and ready for your next step.
The Plan Tab
The Plan tab is where you can view and manage your entire training plan. From here, you can adjust your schedule, manage workouts, and connect compatible devices.
Pace Insights & Estimated Race Times
Review your current performance and past recommendations, and see how you’re tracking towards your goals.
Managing Your Plan
Tapping Manage Plan allows you to:
Adapt your plan: add holidays, B-Races or let us know when you're Not Feeling 100%
Adjust your Training Preferences & Elevation Profile
Adjust your Running Ability, Estimated Race Time and Mileage
Adjust your Running Schedule: set your availability and long run preferences!
Switch your Units of Measure: Set your data units and choose to run to Pace Targets or RPE!
Set up Strength, Yoga or Pilates: Balance your running with complementary training!
Start a new plan, or view recent plans!
Connect Your Devices
Tap Connected Apps to link Strava and Apple Health, sync your calendars, and connect compatible smartwatches and wearable heart rate devices!
The Progress Tab
Workouts
Here you can view all your workouts to date - including free runs and activities outside of your plan.
Use filters to take a deeper dive by workout type, year, or month.
You can also log a manual workout by tapping the + icon in the top-right corner. This is helpful if you’ve experienced GPS inaccuracies and want to link an accurate workout back to your plan!
Performance
Under the Performance section, you can view your weekly and yearly mileage trends, personal records, completed plans, achievements, and all-time stats, as well as your most recent data sources.
The Calendar Tab
The Calendar tab gives you a complete view of your training schedule so you can plan ahead and stay on top of your progress:
Drag and drop workouts within a week or between consecutive weeks to stay organised and flexible.
Review your progress and plan upcoming sessions to optimise your training and recovery.
Whether you're planning your week ahead or reviewing how far you've come, the Training Calendar in the Calendar tab keeps your entire training journey in one place.
The Support Tab

If you’re unsure about anything, or have questions on how to use the Runna app to get the most out of your training, please reach out via our in-app support channel. Our Customer Experience team will do their very best to help!

title: Setting Up and Managing Your Audio Cues

parts.txt: For any workout with set pace targets, you can enable and receive live audio cues from the Runna app via your phone's speaker or compatible running watch. This means you won’t need to look at your watch as often, making training easier and helping you stay focused on your form and surroundings!

🏃 Audio cues are available for running workouts only. They're not currently supported for strength or cross-training sessions — though this is on the roadmap. See How do I turn on audio cues for my strength workouts? in the FAQs below for more detail.
How to Turn on Audio Cues on Your Phone
For the best experience, connect your earphones to your phone to receive live coaching as you run.
In the Runna app, go to Plan → Profile (top-left) → Phone Recording
Make sure Run Splits and Pace Alerts are switched ON
You can also adjust the volume here
Then go to Record Workout → Run Settings (top right) and choose your feedback distance

Run Splits read out your exact pace after each km or mile (e.g., "Lap 1 completed in 5:50 min/km"). Pace Alerts prompt you to speed up or slow down when you're outside your target pace range. Both are recommended for the most detailed audio feedback during your run.
You can also enable Pause Warning to get a voice reminder when your workout is paused and you start moving again. To turn it on/off, go to Profile → Phone Recording Settings → Pause Warning.
Outdoor audio cues include:
Get ready to start (there’s a visual countdown, but no verbal countdown)
Start running
Pace alerts (speed up / slow down)
Pausing / Resuming
Halfway information
Lap x completed in x time
Workout completed in x time
Treadmill audio cues include:
Get ready to start (there’s a visual countdown, but no verbal countdown)
Start running
Pausing / Resuming
Halfway information
Lap x completed in x time, average speed x mph/kph
Workout completed in x time
How to Turn on Audio Cues on Runna Apple Watch App
On your phone:
Open the Runna app and tap Record Workout
Select Outdoor Run
Tap Settings (top right) → Feedback Distance
Set your preferred feedback distance and adjust the volume
On your Apple Watch:
Open the Runna app on your Apple Watch
Swipe right
Make sure Audio Cues are switched ON
You can also adjust cue volume on your watch by opening Settings → Volume and turning the Digital Crown.
Audio cues include
Run splits
Pace alerts (too fast / too slow)
Start / Stop cues
No headphones connected → cues play through the Apple Watch speaker
Headphones connected to Apple Watch → cues play through headphones (music dimmed)
Headphones connected to iPhone → cues play from phone and onwards into your headphones (music dimmed)
Advanced volume control
On your Apple Watch, open Runna.
Go to Settings → Advanced Settings → Use In-App Volume.
Toggle ON.
Force close the app and reopen it — changes won’t apply mid-workout.
Once enabled, go to Settings → Audio Cue Volume and use the slider to set your preferred level.
How to Turn on Audio Cues on Garmin

When using a Garmin device, you’ll receive pace and interval alerts via vibrations and sounds from the watch itself. Depending on your Garmin model, you may also be able to enable audio prompts. Garmin’s available audio cues vary by device and will differ slightly from the cues provided directly by the Runna app on your phone.
If your headphones are connected directly to your Garmin watch:
Pace alerts (based on your Garmin settings)
Too slow / too fast alerts
No "halfway" cue
Next lap information
If your headphones are connected to your phone:
Pace alerts (based on your Garmin settings)
No too slow / too fast alerts
Next lap information
To manage these settings, open the Garmin Connect app, tap your watch icon at the top of the home screen, then go to Audio Prompts and enable:
Workout Alerts
Activity Alerts
Lap Alerts
Pace/Speed Alerts
After making any changes, make sure to refresh the Bluetooth connection to your watch. Feel free to experiment and enable or disable prompts to find what works best for you!
How to Turn on Audio Cues on Suunto
Audio cues are only available on the Suunto 9 Peak Pro and Suunto Vertical. These include:
Slow down/ speed up
Rest
Start running again
Open the Suunto app on your phone.
Go to Watch settings and select your compatible watch.
Navigate to Audio prompts (or Sounds & Alerts, depending on your device).
Make sure audio cues are switched ON.
Connect your Bluetooth headphones directly to your watch (audio cues won’t play through your phone).
Refresh the connection between the Suunto app and your watch to apply the changes.

On smartwatches, enabling the auto-lap feature can interfere with audio cues. Our workouts use carefully placed laps to deliver the right instruction at the right time. If auto-lap is turned on, your watch may move to the next lap early (or add an extra one), meaning your audio cues can change before you’ve completed the distance or rep.
How Do Audio Cues Work on Race Day?
⚠️ Race day pace alerts depend on your course type
Flat or rolling race → Pace alerts (speed up / slow down) ARE active. You will be prompted to adjust your effort to stay within your target pace range.
Moderate or hilly race → Pace alerts are NOT active. You will only receive run splits (e.g., "1 km completed in 5:50 min/km"), because we can't predict the effect of gradients on your pace.
Flat / Rolling Races

For flat or rolling races, if you use the race workout included in your plan, you’ll be given a target pace range. Your audio cues will prompt you to speed up or slow down to stay close to the midpoint of that range.
Expected audio cues:
Pace alerts (speed up / slow down)
Run splits (e.g., “1 km completed in 5:50 min/km”)
To make sure these cues are enabled, go to: Plan → Profile (top-left) → Phone Recording and ensure Run Splits and Pace Alerts are switched ON.
Moderate / Hilly Races

For moderate or hilly courses, Runna will provide run splits as you go (for example, “1 km completed in 5:50 min/km”). To make sure you receive these, go to: Plan → Profile (top-left) → Phone Recording and toggle Run Splits ON.

You won’t receive pace alerts (speed up / slow down) because we can’t predict the inclines and gradients on your course, and factors like gates, narrow paths, or muddy terrain can also affect your pace. We want to avoid encouraging unrealistic targets that could increase injury risk.
You won't receive a countdown before the start of a race workout.
FAQs
Why am I not receiving any audio cues?
This may be because Intervals/Tempo on Track or Open Warm-Up is enabled.
When Intervals/Tempo on Track is on, interval or tempo laps won’t automatically end and you won't receive audio guidance - you'll need to stop these manually.
When Open Warm-Up is on, your warm-up won’t end automatically either - you’ll need to press the Continue or Lap button (depending on your device).
To turn these off, Go to Today → Profile (top-left) → Workouts and toggle OFF:
Intervals/Tempo on Track
Open Warm-Up
Why am I not receiving audio cues to speed up / slow down when recording from my phone?
This could be due to your plan type or app settings.
New to Running (NTR), Return to Running (RTR), and Path to parkrun plans use time-based workouts, so pace alerts aren’t available.
If Open Warm-Up or Intervals/Tempo on Track is enabled, pace alerts won’t trigger automatically. Turn these off via Today → Profile → Workouts.
How do audio cues work during interval and tempo workouts?

During interval and tempo sessions, audio cues fire at lap boundaries — not continuously throughout each rep. You'll hear a cue when each interval or recovery period begins or ends, not ongoing pace feedback mid-rep.
What to expect during intervals:
A cue when each lap boundary is reached (e.g. "Lap 1 completed in x time")
Pace alerts (speed up / slow down) if pace targets are enabled and you're outside your target range
No continuous narration between lap boundaries mid-rep

Make sure Intervals/Tempo on Track is turned OFF. When this setting is enabled, laps don't advance automatically and no audio cues will play during the workout. To check, go to Today → Profile (top-left) → Workouts and toggle Intervals/Tempo on Track OFF.
Why am I receiving intermittent audio cues on my Apple Watch?
This may be due to a setting called 'Cover to Mute'. To disable this, go to your Watch Settings → Gestures → Cover to Mute and turn it OFF.
Are audio cues compatible with Apple Workouts?
Unfortunately not. Due to Apple’s API limitations, Runna’s personalised audio cues can’t be delivered through the Apple Workouts app. However, you will still receive Apple’s built-in notifications:
Interval notifications
Heart rate zone alerts
Split pace notifications
Haptic feedback
For full Runna audio cues, record your workout directly using the Runna Apple Watch app.
Are audio cues compatible with COROS watches?

No, audio cues aren’t supported on COROS watches due to hardware limitations. You can record your run using Runna on your phone alongside your watch, but be aware this may result in conflicting pace or distance data due to separate GPS sources.
Are audio cues compatible with Garmin Venu 2?

No, the Garmin Venu 2 doesn’t support audio cues. You can still receive full coaching and pacing cues by recording your run via the Runna app on your phone, but be aware this may result in conflicting pace or distance data due to separate GPS sources.
Are audio cues compatible with Suunto watches?
Audio cues are only available on:
Suunto 9 Peak Pro
Suunto Vertical

You can still receive full coaching and pacing cues by recording your run via the Runna app on your phone, but be aware this may result in conflicting pace or distance data due to separate GPS sources.
Can I get an alert when my workout pauses?
Yes! You can enable Pause Warning to get a voice reminder when your workout is paused. To turn it on, go to Profile → Phone Recording Settings → Pause Warning.
Why do my audio cues sound robotic?

We’re exploring more natural voice options, but live audio cues (like pace alerts) require real-time processing. Using synthetic voices allows us to deliver cues accurately and without delay, even with limited connectivity!
Why are my audio cues so quiet?
Check your volume settings:
In Runna, go to Plan → Profile (top-left) → Phone Recording → Volume and set it to Loud (100%).
On iPhone, go to Settings → Sounds & Haptics → Headphone Safety and try turning OFF Reduce Loud Audio. This can improve volume and clarity!
Why are my audio cues in a different language?
Audio cues are delivered in the same language as your Runna app settings. Changing the voice (e.g. System Default, Monica, Paulina) changes the tone - not the language.
To change the language in Runna: Go to Today → Profile → Language Settings.
iOS (change voice): Go to Today → Profile → Phone Recording → Voice.

Android (change voice + language): Runna uses your phone’s text-to-speech settings. Go to Settings → Accessibility → Text-to-Speech and select your preferred language and voice. This helps prevent cues playing in different languages.
How do I turn on audio cues for my strength workouts?
There isn't audio cues yet for strength workouts, but we're working on it!
How can I change how often I receive distance feedback?
Feedback distance can be adjusted for free runs only, it can't be changed for guided plan sessions. To adjust it for a free run:
Tap Record Workout
Select Outdoor Run
Tap the settings gear (top right)
Adjust your Feedback Distance
For guided plan sessions, feedback distance is fixed and can't be customised.
Any questions?
If you have any further questions or need more support with your audio cues, please don’t hesitate to reach out via the Support Tab!

title: How to Update My Plan Version and Access New Features

parts.txt: At Runna, we’re always rolling out new features to make your training plans more adaptable and customizable. Sometimes these updates can affect your current plan, which isn’t always ideal.

With Plan Versions, you can choose when to update your plan and accept changes - and if you don’t like the update, you can easily revert back to the original version. This way, you stay in control, and your plan only changes when you’re ready.
Accessing Plan Versions
Open the Runna App and go to the Plan tab.
Select Manage Plan.

Just below the name of your plan, you’ll see a status pill showing one of two options:Plan Up To Date: You’re on the newest version of your plan.New Plan Version Available: A newer version of your plan is ready to update.
Plan Up To Date: You’re on the newest version of your plan.
New Plan Version Available: A newer version of your plan is ready to update.
If the ‘Plan Versions’ pill isn’t available under ‘Manage Plan’ you may need to update your app.
Updating Your Plan Version
Tap the New Plan Version Available pill.
On the next screen, you’ll see:Your current Plan VersionThe new Plan Version availableA summary of what the update includes
Your current Plan Version
The new Plan Version available
A summary of what the update includes
To update your plan, tap Update.
Your plan will then be updated, and any new features released since you first created your plan will now be available.
Updating your Plan Version may cause changes to your upcoming training.
Reverting to a Previous Plan Version
On the Manage Plan page, under your plan name, tap Plan Up To Date.
Select Revert to Previous Version.

Important: Plan Versions only allows you to revert to a previous version after updating your plan using the steps above. It does not allow you to revert your plan after you'd made any manual changes (e.g., updating your estimated 5K time).
FAQs
What if I don’t see ‘Plan Up To Date’ or ‘New Plan Version Available’ under ‘Manage Plan’?
You may not see your Plan Version pill for one of the following reasons:
App Version: Make sure you’re using version 8.15.0 or later
Plan Type: Plan Versions is only available for race plans and distance-based goal plans (e.g., 10K improvement plans, marathons).
I don’t like the new version of my plan. Can I revert it back?

Yes! You can revert your plan to the previous version if you’re unhappy with the update. Go to Plan → Tap Manage Plan → Tap Plan Version (under the name of your plan)→ Revert (this only works for version updates, not manual Manage Plan changes)
What features will updating my Plan Version unlock?
This depends on when you created your plan. Previous examples include Holiday Mode and Training Preferences!
Can I revert my plan after updating other plan details under ‘Manage Plan’?

No. Plan Versions only enables you to revert your plan having updated it via ‘New Plan Version Available’. It does not revert any manual changes you make to your running ability, elevation profile or other inputs under Manage Plan.

If you want to revert changes to those fields, you’ll need to manually update them back to their previous values. For example, if you changed your Running Ability from Intermediate to Advanced, you can change it back to Intermediate.
Need more support?
If you have any questions or need more support, please reach out via the in-app support tab and we'll do our best to help!
